name: English
title: Free DISC Personality Test — Online, 10 Minutes, No Sign-Up
description: Free DISC personality test: 24 questions, 10 minutes, no sign-up. Find your dominant style, strengths and growth areas. Instant result, also by email.

addon.D: more drive, speed and readiness to take responsibility
addon.I: more sociability, optimism and the ability to inspire people
addon.S: more patience, reliability and attention to the team
addon.C: more precision, caution and reliance on facts

blocks.I: I like being the center of attention

blocks.D: I say exactly what I think
I get straight to the point

blocks.S: I accept things as they are

strengths: You make decisions quickly and take responsibility for them
You keep your footing in a crisis and act when others hesitate
You set ambitious goals and achieve them
growth: Impatience with people who work more slowly or carefully
A tendency to push a decision through without hearing alternatives
Bluntness that others experience as pressure
motivation: Authority and the ability to influence how things go
D.stress: Under pressure you become harder and less tolerant: you interrupt, take everything on yourself and bypass rules for the sake of speed. Clear authority and room to act independently help.
communication: Keep it short and to the point: results, deadlines, options
Don't drag out the introduction or beat around the bush
Offer a choice rather than a ready-made answer: deciding for themselves matters
D.environment: A dynamic environment with a lot of autonomy, clear goals and a direct link between effort and results. Routine and tight supervision are demotivating.

strengths: You connect with people easily and win them over
You inspire and motivate the team
You generate ideas and see opportunities where others see problems
You stay optimistic in difficult situations
growth: Promises made in the heat of the moment that are hard to keep later
Not enough attention to details and deadlines
A tendency to talk more than listen
I.stress: Under pressure you become scattered and impulsive, avoid unpleasant conversations and may overestimate how things stand. Open discussion and support from colleagues help.
communication: Start with a personal connection, not the agenda
Give room to speak up and discuss ideas
Put agreements in writing: it helps both sides
I.environment: An open, friendly environment with plenty of contact, recognition and freedom from rigid procedures. Isolation and monotony drain the energy.

strengths: You can be relied on over the long haul
You know how to listen to and support others
You bring the team together and defuse conflicts
growth: Resistance to change, even beneficial change
Difficulty saying no and standing your ground
Keeping disagreement to yourself to preserve the peace
motivation: Clear expectations and rules of the game
S.stress: Under pressure you withdraw, become overly accommodating and put off decisions. Sudden change and open conflict are especially hard to bear. Time to adjust and a calm conversation help.
communication: Give advance notice of changes and explain why they are needed
Ask for their opinion directly: they rarely volunteer it
Don't push or rush them for an answer
S.environment: A stable environment with clear processes, good relationships and a reasonable pace of change. Chaos, constant switching and aggressive competition are exhausting.

strengths: High quality of work and attention to detail
The ability to think through risks and plan ahead
growth: Perfectionism and missed deadlines in pursuit of the ideal
Excessive criticism of yourself and others
Retreating into analysis instead of acting
C.stress: Under pressure you withdraw into yourself, become overly critical and get stuck in details. Having to act without data is irritating. Clear criteria and time to verify help.
communication: Allow time to think it over; don't demand an answer right away
Criticize specifically and on the merits, without emotion
C.environment: A structured environment with clear standards, access to information and the ability to work with focus. Uncertainty, haste and emotional pressure reduce effectiveness.

D.name: Achiever
D.summary: You move toward the goal directly and fast: you take the initiative, decide without lengthy discussion and aren't afraid of resistance. Being in control and seeing measurable results matters to you.

I.name: Inspirer
I.summary: You work through people: you make connections easily, spread enthusiasm and persuade with words and mood. Recognition and lively interaction matter to you, while formalities and routine wear you out quickly.

S.name: Anchor
S.summary: You create stability: you keep your word, finish what you start, support people and smooth over conflicts. Predictability, trust and time to get used to change matter to you.

C.name: Analyst
C.summary: You rely on facts and standards: you check, analyze, plan and dislike hasty decisions. Quality and being right matter to you more than speed and outward effect.

DI.name: Pioneer
DI.summary: Drive and charm: you lead quickly toward the goal and know how to bring people along. You persuade with momentum and enthusiasm and decide on the go, but patience for details and caution often run short.

DC.name: Strategist
DC.summary: Results through quality: you are demanding of yourself and others, think systematically and never decide without arguments. Strong on complex tasks, but you can come across as cold and overly critical.

DS.name: Practitioner
DS.summary: Persistence and reliability: you push steadily toward the goal without any fuss and finish what you start. You value independence and stability at the same time, which is a rare combination.

ID.name: Motivator
ID.summary: Energy and drive: you infect people with ideas and aren't afraid to take the initiative. You easily sell ideas and goals, but risk overestimating your strength and underestimating the details.

IS.name: Mentor
IS.summary: Warmth and involvement: you win people over, and know how to support and unite them. Relationships and atmosphere matter to you, while conflict and harsh demands are hard to take.

IC.name: Presenter
IC.summary: Eloquence and precision: you can convincingly present a well-thought-out position. You combine sociability with attention to facts, but may waver between spontaneity and caution.

SI.name: Diplomat
SI.summary: Calm and friendliness: you create an atmosphere of trust, smooth over rough edges and support the team. Saying no and defending an unpopular decision is hard for you.

SC.name: Specialist
SC.summary: Reliability and accuracy: you work methodically, follow the rules and see things through without haste. You value stability and clear expectations, while abrupt change and pressure are hard to bear.

SD.name: Implementer
SD.summary: Perseverance and patience: you calmly but firmly drive things to a result without getting caught up in needless discussion. Reliable over the long haul, though from the outside you may seem stubborn.

CD.name: Perfectionist
CD.summary: Standards and willpower: you demand precision from yourself and others, spot mistakes quickly and aren't afraid to point them out. Strong on complex expert tasks, but you can be too strict and closed off.

CS.name: Expert
CS.summary: Precision and consistency: you work thoughtfully, check the details and rely on proven methods. A dependable specialist who finds uncertainty and rapid change hard to handle.

CI.name: Consultant
CI.summary: Analysis and connection: you can get to the bottom of a question and explain it to others in plain terms. A rare combination: caution in conclusions and ease in communication. Sometimes the inner tug-of-war between "verify" and "share" gets in the way.

ui.intro.h1: Free DISC test: how you act, communicate and make decisions
ui.intro.lead: DISC describes four styles of behavior. Everyone has all four, but to different degrees. The test will show your dominant style, your strengths, your growth areas and how others can work with you best.
ui.intro.howText: Each of the 24 blocks has four statements. Mark the one that describes you most and the one that describes you least. Answer the way you usually behave at work, not the way you would like to. Don't overthink it: your first reaction is the most accurate.
ui.intro.emailLabel: Email address to send your result to
ui.intro.emailHint: When you finish the test, your result will be emailed to this address.
ui.intro.nameRequired: Please enter your first and last name
ui.intro.emailRequired: Please enter a valid email address
ui.test.hint: Mark one statement in each column and press “{next}”. You can change your choice until you move on.
ui.report.flat: Your profile is balanced: no single style stands out strongly. This usually means behavioral flexibility, but it can sometimes indicate uncertainty in the answers. The dominant style was determined by the highest score.
ui.report.howto: How to read this. The overall profile is the difference between your "most" and "least" answers. The public self is how you try to behave at work. The natural self is how you behave when you're not thinking about it. Values above the midpoint (50%) are considered pronounced.
ui.report.secondaryAddon: It adds {addon} to your dominant style.

ui.pages.styles.title: The Four DISC Styles: D, I, S, C — Traits, Strengths, Motivation
ui.pages.styles.description: A detailed description of the four DISC behavioral styles: Dominance, Influence, Steadiness, Conscientiousness. Traits, strengths, growth areas, motivation and behavior under stress.
ui.pages.styles.lead: DISC describes behavior on four scales. Everyone has all four styles, but one or two are more pronounced. Below: what is typical of each style, what motivates it and how to communicate with it.
ui.pages.profiles.title: 16 DISC Profiles — Descriptions of the DISC Personality Types
ui.pages.profiles.description: All 16 profiles of the DISC test: four pure styles and twelve combinations. A short description of each type and a link to its detailed page.
ui.pages.profiles.lead: The test result is your dominant style and, if it is pronounced, a secondary one. That gives 16 profiles: four pure styles and twelve combinations. Find yours, or take the test to discover it.

ui.consent.label: Cookie notice
ui.consent.text: This site uses cookies and similar technologies: your browser's local storage keeps your progress, result and chosen language. The hosting provider (GitHub Pages) and the font service (Google Fonts) receive technical data such as your IP address and browser type. Your test result is sent only to the email address you provide.
ui.consent.details: Stored in your browser: the name and job title you enter before the test; your answers and unfinished progress; your latest result; your chosen language; a note that you have seen this notice. The data stays on your device only and is removed when you clear the site's data in your browser. Third-party services: GitHub Pages (hosting) and Google Fonts (fonts) receive standard technical request data. No analytics or advertising trackers are used. When you finish the test, your name, email address and answers are passed to the email-sending service (Google Apps Script) in order to send you your result; they are not used for anything else.
